submission.justification: R1 at 3 cm gives the best separation I measured for R1 (3.86 sigma). Separation peaks near 3 cm and falls at larger thickness (2.79 sigma at 6 cm). R2 gave a higher separation in the 2025 study (4.6 sigma at 3 cm), but I did not re-simulate it. The specs describe R2 as porous with no hydrophobic treatment. Porous material without that treatment may absorb moisture and degrade, and the documents contain no aging data to rule this out. The dry-nitrogen flush is documented only for operation, so it does not cover storage or downtime. R1 is the hydrophobic-treated porous option, so I chose it as the one most likely to keep its performance over the lifetime. Its lifetime performance is also not directly demonstrated. If aging data show R2 is stable, R2 would give about 0.8 sigma more separation and should be reconsidered.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pi/K separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R1 scanned over 2-6 cm; maximum is 3.86 sigma at 3 cm. R2 is higher (4.6 sigma in 2025) but its lifetime is unverified, so this is the best among the options I consider lifetime-safe.

requirements.requirement: Radiator is one of the three candidates

requirements.evidence: No aging or humidity data in the documents. R1 has a hydrophobic treatment, which is a favorable indicator. R2 has no stated protection. Nitrogen flush is documented only for operation.
